_why: O-HYPERDRIVE-COLLISION. Every Cloudflare Hyperdrive configuration a Worker binds opens its OWN pool of connections to
the origin Postgres, and the origin has a fixed number to give. This file is the one place a configuration's
connection cap is declared, and tooling/ci/assert-hyperdrive-cap.mjs refuses a wrangler `hyperdrive` binding without
a row here, and a set of caps that adds up to more than `origin.budget`.
WHY THE CAP HAS TO BE DECLARED BEFORE THE BINDING EXISTS, NOT AFTER. Hyperdrive's origin connection limit is a SOFT
limit: Cloudflare's limits page says a client that cannot reach an existing pool gets a new pool with its own
allocation, so 'connection counts may occasionally exceed the listed limits' (paid plan ~100 per configuration,
free ~20). The per-configuration knob is `wrangler hyperdrive create|update --origin-connection-limit <n>`, 'the
(soft) maximum number of connections that Hyperdrive may establish to the origin database'. Nothing sets it by
default, so an unset configuration may take up to the plan ceiling, and against the budget below that is more
connections than Box A has free.
⏱ 2026-09-14 — NO CONFIGURATION EXISTS YET. `git grep -nliE "hyperdrive|max_connections"` over the whole tree
returned zero files before this file and its guard landed, so `configs` is empty on purpose, and the guard passes
over zero bindings while printing that count. The first binding reddens CI until it has a row here.
⏱ 2026-09-22 — THE ORIGIN NUMBERS ARE MEASURED ON BOX A, AND `inUse` IS A CEILING, NOT A SAMPLE. They were read after
the owner-delegated Postgres restart that raised max_connections from the built-in default: `pg_settings` reports
`max_connections` with source `command line` (a `-c` in the db service's compose override, which beats every conf
file), and superuser_reserved_connections is unchanged. `inUse` is how many connections the Supabase services on
Box A are ALLOWED to open, with GoTrue's pool capped by GOTRUE_DB_MAX_POOL_SIZE (read back from its startup log), not
how many they held at the moment of reading. A sample lets the caps below grow into slots Supabase's own pools may
still take. The old `verify` counted every pg_stat_activity row, background processes that hold no slot included;
the new one counts client backends. Raising `budget` further is another Postgres restart in the owner's window,
with the tracked copy of the override in Private runbooks/config/ edited to match.

origin.asOf: measured 2026-09-22 03:26Z on Box A after the max_connections change; inUse is the CEILING the Supabase services may open (18 held at measurement), not a sample
origin.verify: on Box A: SELECT setting, source FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('max_connections','superuser_reserved_connections'); SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type='client backend';
